core.title: Ship a route-control runner with its train-resolution entry point when the journey map declares interlocking routes
core.given: The consumer's composition root declares, in its action-to-route mapping (the journey map), at least one interlocking route - a guarded-route value rather than a direct train reference
core.when: the consumer is changed or checked (any file, whenever the route was added)
core.then: Ship a route-control runner as a scanned source file in the tree the profile designates for it, exposing the train-resolution entry point.
prefer: Ship one runner component whose construction accepts a reference to the route definitions and whose entry point accepts the action, its inputs and optional state, and returns a resolution.
The entry point evaluates guarded routes, resolves exactly one admissible train, then delegates execution to the train runner.
avoid: Interlocking routes in the journey map with no route-control runner at all.
A route-control runner without the train-resolution entry point.
A runner outside the designated tree, or present only in excluded generated/vendored trees (never scanned).
unless: Pure direct-train consumer: no interlocking route in the journey map and no route-control runner.
core.why: An interlocking is executable only as a route-control component: its entry point evaluates guarded routes and picks one admissible train before delegation, so without it declared routes cannot run.
evidence: If any journey-map value in the composition root is an interlocking route, a route-control runner exists in a scanned source file of the designated tree and declares the train-resolution entry point.
verification: Standing repository-state check: evaluated on the current repository state, not only on newly added routes, and it applies whichever file changed.

Flag when an interlocking route is declared in the journey map but no route-control runner is shipped in the designated tree, or the runner lacks the train-resolution entry point; compliance is shown by the stack's check for this rule reporting no finding.

An eligible runner is a scanned source file of the tree the profile designates for it: the profile supplies the journey-map idiom, the runner component and its tree, the scanned source file suffix and the excluded trees; which files are inspected and how the journey map, the runner and the entry point are recognized is the per-stack detector's concern.
Never scan the profile's excluded generated/vendored trees; a runner found only there does not satisfy the rule.
Do not flag a pure direct-train consumer: no interlocking route in the journey map and no route-control runner.
Severity 4, disposition strict: a finding is not suppressible and fails CI.

fires: The journey map currently contains an interlocking route and no route-control runner exists in the designated tree - including a pre-existing violation and a change touching only the composition root.
An interlocking route is declared, a route-control runner exists, but it exposes no train-resolution entry point.
A change introduces a new interlocking route into the journey map.
An interlocking route is declared and the only route-control runner lives in an excluded generated/vendored tree: excluded files never count as an eligible runner, so the rule still fires.
doesNotFire: A pure direct-train consumer: every journey-map value is a direct train reference and no route-control runner exists.

Scan exclusion: files in the profile's excluded generated/vendored trees are never scanned and never count as an eligible runner (this does not exempt a declared interlocking route that lacks an eligible runner).

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the composition root lives; the file whose journey map declares the routes.
The composition root's action-to-route mapping construct (the journey map) itself; its placement is given by roles.composition_root.path.
How a journey-map value that routes through an interlocking (a guarded route) is distinguished from a direct train reference.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a JOURNEY_MAP value that is an {interlockingId, path} route object (interlocking route), vs a direct trainId string (direct train)

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's route-control component and the tree in which it must be shipped; the eligible files of that tree are its scanned source files (their suffix is suffix.source).
profileRequirements.bunValue: a `class InterlockingRunner` under `src/trains/**`; the route-control component that selects one admissible train and delegates execution to TrainRunner

profileRequirements.meaning: The runner's entry point that evaluates guarded routes and resolves exactly one admissible train before delegation.
The file suffix of scanned production source; an eligible runner is a scanned source file of the designated tree.
Generated/vendored trees the check never scans; a runner found only there is not an eligible runner.

neutralityNotes: ATDD domain vocabulary (journey map, interlocking, interlocking route, train, train runner) is kept in the core: these are approach-level concepts, and the urn group already recognizes train and journey as artifact kinds. Placement of the journey map comes from the existing roles.composition_root.path key and the scanned source-file restriction from the existing suffix.source key, combined in core:verification with the designated runner tree; only the mapping construct, its value taxonomy, the runner component/tree and the entry point needed proposed idiom keys. core:prefer[0] adds no guidance beyond the Bun example: it neutralizes only its shape (construction accepts a reference to the route definitions; the entry point takes the action, its inputs and optional state and returns a resolution), and core:prefer[1] carries the resolve-then-delegate semantics that bun.json states explicitly. Detector, family and finding ids of this rule, the regex-over-source mechanism, the language-scoping activation fact, the concrete path globs and the code example are bunOnly. Per-rule severity 4 and strict disposition are kept in core:verification, and the exclusion deference (never scan the profile's excluded trees; a runner only there is ineligible) is preserved there rather than in the profile.
